title: A namespaced Policy can no longer make an apiCall outside its own namespace (1.15.3, 1.16.3, 1.17.0)
quote: fix: prevent cross-namespace access in apiCall
remediation: In a namespaced `Policy` every context `apiCall.urlPath` must name the policy's own namespace: a path into another namespace, a path with no namespace segment (cluster-scoped resources, cluster-wide lists) and every `apiCall.service` call are refused ("path ... refers to namespace ..., which is different from the policy namespace", "path ... does not contain a namespace segment, which is required for namespaced policies"). There is no opt-out. Move such a rule into a ClusterPolicy scoped with `match.resources.namespaces`, or keep the lookup inside the policy's namespace. ClusterPolicies are not affected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace as $ns | select([.. | objects | .apiCall? // empty | objects] | any((.service != null) or ((.urlPath // "") | test("/namespaces/" + $ns + "(/|$)") | not))) | "Policy \($ns)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a namespaced Policy whose apiCall calls a service or a path that does not literally name its own namespace (a path built from a variable is listed too: check what it resolves to)

title: A rule's context is capped at 2Mi by default (1.15.3, 1.16.3, 1.17.0)

detection.reason: the size of the data a rule loads is only known when it runs

remediation: ClusterPolicy / Policy rules that load more than 2Mi into their context (a cluster-wide `apiCall` list, a large ConfigMap or GlobalContextEntry) now fail with "context size limit exceeded: N bytes exceeds limit of N bytes". Narrow the call (a namespaced path, a `jmesPath` that keeps only what the rule reads) or raise the limit: key `maxContextSize` in the `kyverno` ConfigMap, chart value `config.maxContextSize` (a quantity; the string `"0"` disables the check — an unquoted 0 is dropped by the chart).
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .context? // empty | arrays | .[] | select(.apiCall != null or .globalReference != null or .configMap != null)] | .[0] != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row loads API, global-context or ConfigMap data into a rule context — the entries that can exceed the limit

title: A namespaced Policy can only read ConfigMaps in its own namespace (1.16.4, 1.17.2, 1.18.0)
quote: restrict configmap access for namespaced policies
remediation: In a namespaced `Policy` a context `configMap` entry that names another namespace is refused ("configMap namespace ... is different from policy namespace ..."), and an entry with NO namespace now reads the policy's namespace — it used to read `default`. A shared lookup ConfigMap in `default`, `kyverno` or any other namespace stops resolving. Copy the ConfigMap into the policy's namespace, or move the rule into a ClusterPolicy. ClusterPolicies are not affected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace as $ns | select([.. | objects | .context? // empty | arrays | .[] | .configMap? // empty | objects] | any((.namespace // "") != $ns)) | "Policy \($ns)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a namespaced Policy reading a ConfigMap with no namespace set or one that is not literally its own

title: Service calls from policies carry a scoped token with audience `kyverno-svc.kyverno.io` (1.16.4, 1.17.2, 1.18.0)

detection.reason: how the called services authenticate Kyverno is outside the cluster objects collected

quote: fix: use scoped token for request authz
remediation: Kyverno no longer sends its own ServiceAccount token to the services policies call. `apiCall.service` requests (and, from 1.18.0, CEL `http.Get` / `http.Post`) carry a separate projected token with audience `kyverno-svc.kyverno.io`, mounted at /var/run/secrets/kyverno/apicall/token from the `apicall-token` volume the chart adds (1 h expiry). A service that authenticates the caller by TokenReview against the API server's default audience starts rejecting the call: accept the new audience there, or set chart value `apiCallToken.audience` (`""` restores the cluster's default audience). Manifests not rendered by the chart must add the projected volume — without it the request is sent with no Authorization header.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | .apiCall? // empty | objects | .service? // empty] | .[0] != null) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row makes an apiCall.service call

title: MutatingPolicies with CEL compilation errors are refused (1.15.2, 1.16.0)
quote: Fixed issue to block mutating policies upon compilation errors (#13972)
remediation: Fix MutatingPolicies whose CEL does not compile; they are refused on the next create/update.
verifyCommand: kubectl get mutatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.status.conditionStatus.ready // true) == false) | .metadata.name'  # each row is a MutatingPolicy Kyverno reports not ready

title: HTTP calls are disabled by default in namespaced CEL policies (CVE-2026-4789; 1.16.4, 1.17.2)
quote: [backport] chore(security): disable HTTP in namespaced policies by default (CVE-2026-4789)
remediation: Namespaced CEL policies that call `http.Get`/`http.Post` stop compiling, so they stop enforcing. Move the call to a cluster-scoped policy, or re-enable it cluster-wide with `--allowHTTPInNamespacedPolicies=true` (env `FLAG_ENABLE_HTTP_IN_NAMESPACED_POLICIES`) on the admission and cleanup controllers — there is no per-namespace switch.
verifyCommand: kubectl get $(kubectl api-resources --api-group=policies.kyverno.io -o name | grep '^namespaced' | paste -sd, -) -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("http[.](Get|Post)")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a namespaced CEL policy that makes an HTTP call (only the kinds this cluster serves are listed)

title: Chart values moved: `templating.*` → `global.templating.*`, `cleanupController.webhookServer.port` → `cleanupController.server.port`
quote: Fixed to make helm templating value global (#14144)
remediation: Move `templating.*` under `global.templating.*` and a cleanup-controller `webhookServer.port` override to `cleanupController.server.port` (#13714, values-key diff v1.15.3 → v1.16.4). Helm ignores the old keys silently — a hostNetwork port override is dropped.
verifyCommand: helm list -A -o json | jq -r '.[] | select(.chart | test("^kyverno-[0-9]")) | "\(.namespace)/\(.name) \(.chart) app \(.app_version)"'  # each row is a Kyverno Helm release; read its values with: helm get values NAME -n NAMESPACE
coversNotes: v1.16.0 Added: Supported bind to a hostIP when in hostNetwork
